opening.headline: After explaining why costs continue to increase even after budget alerts are triggered, it attributes the difference to alerts versus limitations.
body: Even after receiving an email indicating that the budget threshold has been exceeded, costs often significantly overrun by the end of the month. This is because the alert only notifies personnel and does not halt usage.

In this class, we examine Databricks budgets and block usage, Snowflake resource monitoring and budgets, as well as user-level quotas, distinguishing exactly which expenses each method covers. We review alerts to analyze overage cases and confirm how to pair two such mechanisms.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the difference between budget alerts and actual usage limitations
Databricks budget, Snowflake resource monitoring, and query scope differentiation

screens.title: Budget alerts have come in, but costs have continued to rise.
screens.lead: After reading the situation where the monthly expenses exceeded the budget despite receiving a budget alert, consider what might have been missed.

visual.alt: This is a line graph showing that cumulative costs continue to rise even after an alert has been triggered at the monthly budget threshold.
labels: Dates from the beginning to the end of the month
Continue using after alert is dismissed

paragraphs: An email arrived indicating that the budget threshold was exceeded mid-month. The responsible party reviewed the email and shared it across the team channel. However, agent app calls continued to increase, and by the end of the month, costs had significantly surpassed the budget.

What happened, then? Email notifications are merely devices that inform people about a situation; they are not devices that stop usage. If the person receiving the notification is unable to respond immediately or lacks a way to respond, usage continues as before.

The means of cost control can be broadly categorized into two types: notification-based methods and actual enforcement methods. Since these two types often appear together in the same settings menu, it is easy to mistakenly assume that cost control has been completed simply by setting up notifications.

This course clearly distinguishes between budget alerts and actual usage limits, and differentiates among Databricks budgets, Snowflake resource monitoring and budget, and user-specific query quotas in terms of the expenditures they cover.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: This course's alert refers to notifications such as email, while restriction means actions that actually block or halt requests or warehouses.

screens.title: Did you set alerts and restrictions separately?
screens.lead: Think about your organization's cost allocation. You don't need to enter an answer; when you select a question, the instructor's perspective will be revealed.

items.prompt: Does our configuration inform the user or does it block the request?
items.answer: If the settings screen contains only thresholds and recipient lists, then it is an alert configuration. To disable usage, there must be a separate option to block or stop the operation. First, check whether your settings include an option to specify actions.

items.prompt: What impact does restriction have on the service?
items.answer: Instead of controlling costs, limitations cause the system to reject user requests. Therefore, limitations must be carefully designed regarding which users and which scopes are affected, and how to guide users when a limitation is applied. If having no limitations is risky, then having overly broad limitations is also risky.

items.prompt: What happens if the person who receives the alert is on vacation?
items.answer: Alerts are based on the premise of human intervention. No action occurs if the recipient is not present. The system should be designed to operate with or without a recipient present, or with multiple recipients.

screens.outro: Now I will check each capability of the two platforms one by one. First, Databricks.

screens.title: Databricks Budget: Alerts and Block Usage
screens.lead: When you hover over or select the terms highlighted in the text, a description appears. Review the structure of the budget by checking each term one at a time.

visual.alt: This is a screen that displays scope, monthly threshold, email, and Block usage check boxes in the Databricks budget setup page.

data.text: Databricks budgets track spending across the entire account or narrow the scope to specific workspaces and Resource tags to track expenses by team and project. Amounts are calculated in USD at list prices. Account administrators create budgets, and workspace administrators manage budgets within the scope of workspaces they administer. Shared threshold can have up to four thresholds, each with a monthly amount and a list of email addresses to receive alerts. If the email list is cleared, alerts are no longer sent, but the budget status can still be viewed in the console. Checking Block usage at a threshold prevents additional requests via Unity Gateway when the limit is reached. A Unity Gateway budget can also include User-specific thresholds. This value is applied individually per user, preventing any single user from monopolizing the entire budget and enabling customized spending limits for specific users or groups.

terms.tip: Up to four can be assigned per budget. Each threshold includes a monthly amount and an email list, and optionally block usage as well.
When checked, additional requests through Unity Gateway are blocked when the threshold is reached. Unlike a threshold that only sends an email, this action actually stops usage.
Pay-Per-Token, AI query batching inference, and external model usage are endpoints that incur costs. Block usage applies to requests on this path.

In the Unity Gateway budget, the same amount is applied separately to each user. When the limit is reached, a notification is sent, and depending on the selection, only that user's requests can be blocked.
The scope of budget tracking is narrowed down to usage tagged with specific tags. In Unity Gateway budgeting, this contrasts with endpoint tags. Tag names should not contain sensitive information.

screens.outro: Databricks provides a structure that allows users to select both alerts and blocking settings on a single screen. Now let's examine Snowflake's capabilities.

screens.title: Snowflake Resource Monitor and budget
screens.lead: Select each tab one at a time to compare Snowflake's three control mechanisms, including what they report and the actions they take.

tabs.label: Resource Monitor
tabs.body: Resource Monitor watches the usage of credits for virtual warehouses and the cloud services that support them. A credit quota is the amount of credits allowed within a specified period, and after the period ends, usage is reset to zero. Monitor types include account monitor (one per account) that views the entire account, and warehouse monitor that views a specific warehouse. Actions that can be configured include Notify, Suspend, and Suspend Immediately; if no action is specified, no event occurs even when a threshold is reached. Creation is performed by the ACCOUNTADMIN role.

tabs.label: Resource Monitor example
limits of scope
tabs.body: The Resource Monitor only applies to the warehouse. Expenses generated by serverless functions and AI services cannot be tracked using the Resource Monitor. Therefore, AI service consumption must be monitored through alternative means. Even if warehouse costs are well covered by the Resource Monitor, Cortex call costs may still increase outside of this configuration.

tabs.label: budget
tabs.body: A budget sets a monthly spending limit for a group of resources defined by an account or user, and sends alerts when spending is expected to or actually exceeds this limit. Both resource budgets and shared resource budgets allow you to attach stored procedures that execute based on threshold ratios, enabling direct implementation of actions beyond just alerts. However, evaluations occur periodically, so actions typically take up to eight hours to be applied after a threshold is exceeded, and up to two hours with delay optimization enabled.

tabs.label: User-specific quota
tabs.body: Per-user quotas are credit limits applied individually to each user. Unlike budgets, they can restrict usage without requiring the creation of custom stored procedures, and they provide the only built-in blocking mechanism among AI cost control features, with evaluations occurring within a few minutes. Each user's quota is applied separately and does not aggregate. For example, assigning 100 credits to 10 users individually allows a total maximum of 1,000 credits across all users. Since blocking occurs immediately after expenditure, users may exceed their quota slightly.

screens.outro: Having examined the capabilities of the two platforms, we will now address only the case of alerts, and examine beyond that scenario.

screens.title: Only alerts with no restrictions, exceeding cases
screens.lead: The instructor analyzes the introduction case step by step. Click the next arrow to proceed step by step and follow the root cause and improvement measures.

steps.title: Check configuration status
steps.body: An alert for monthly budget was set up in the agent app. Monthly threshold and email recipients were specified, but no action was defined to disable the alert. Only the alert settings were filled in the configuration screen, while the disable options remained empty.

steps.title: Day 1: Notification was sent but no response was received.
steps.body: An alert email was sent on the day the threshold was reached. However, the recipient list contained only one person, who was on vacation. Although the alert functioned properly, no one read it, so no one responded.

steps.title: Later: calls continued and costs increased.
steps.body: Since there was no mechanism to terminate the call, the invocation continued uninterrupted. The app operated normally without knowing that its budget had already been exceeded. Even if a single user or automation process amplified the call, there was no way to stop it, resulting in a billing statement that exceeded the monthly limit significantly.

steps.title: Cause Summary
steps.body: Alerts are based on the premise of human intervention. Without human presence or with delayed response, nothing stops. The root cause of this issue is not a defect in the alerting mechanism, but rather in the design that enables alerts to be set up without imposing any constraints.

steps.title: Improvement: Restricted operations and individual limits
steps.body: Databricks checks block usage against thresholds to prevent additional requests through Unity Gateway, and separately enforces per-user thresholds to block individual user overages. Snowflake uses the resource monitor's suspend functionality in warehouses and applies budget-based stored procedures or per-user query limits in AI services. Alert thresholds are set lower than restriction thresholds to ensure human operators are notified first, and multiple recipients are designated for alerts. Finally, it is essential to predefine the message users receive when limits are reached and who has the authority to lift those limits in order to prevent sudden service outages.

steps.title: Check: Verify after improvement
steps.body: After making changes, verify three things: whether the action restriction is actually set at the threshold, whether alerts are being received by a single recipient, and whether the delay until the restriction takes effect is within an acceptable tolerance. If the delay is too long, lower the threshold below its limit to provide a buffer.

screens.outro: Finally, let's take a quick look at how various means cover various expenditures.

screens.title: What means cover what expenditures?
screens.lead: Read the table from top to bottom and compare each method's scope and limitations. Note that expenditures outside the scope cannot be prevented by any method.

data.notes: Spending outside the defined scope cannot be prevented by any means. For example, a resource monitor tied solely to a warehouse cannot prevent AI service consumption, and the Unity Gateway budget does not cover expenditures that occur outside the Unity Gateway path. Therefore, spending categories must first be listed, and alerts and limits must be paired accordingly. Additionally, due to differing evaluation cycles, the delay before limits are applied varies by method. A Snowflake budget typically takes up to eight hours, while user-specific quotas may take only a few minutes. For this reason, designs often apply limits at a ratio below 100% of a monthly budget rather than at 100%. Furthermore, the last column of a table being empty does not mean that a method lacks limit capabilities—it may instead mean that the limit must be implemented directly, so this must be interpreted carefully.

screens.outro: Now let's summarize the entire lesson.

screens.title: Key points and reflection
screens.lead: We organize the course content around the difference between alerts and restrictions. Please review your organization's settings while reading this.

paragraphs: Alerts notify, but limits stop. A control that only provides alerts operates only when a person responds at the right time, and thus cannot ensure cost containment.

Databricks budget combines scope, monthly thresholds, email lists, and block usage. Block usage prevents additional requests to the Unity Gateway path, and per-user thresholds prevent any single user from gaining exclusive access.

Snowflake allocates resource monitoring to warehouses and budgets to serverless and AI services. User query throttling can occur automatically and more quickly than budget limits, but remember that these limits do not aggregate.

Appropriate control measures must be matched to the type of expenditure. Expenditures outside the scope cannot be prevented by any means. The design must also account for the varying delays between when control measures are implemented and when their limitations take effect.

Going back to the introductory example, what was needed was not more alerts, but rather thresholds with corresponding limiting actions and per-user limits. Alerts are mechanisms designed for users, while limits are mechanisms designed for the system; by co-designing both, cost control is achieved. Create a table pairing one alert with one limit for each expenditure category and review it—empty cells directly indicate our vulnerabilities.

callout.text: In our control, are there only alerts, or are there actual mechanisms that stop processes? Please verify one by one according to expenditure type.

checks.q: When does Databricks budget reach its threshold, how to actually block additional requests through Unity Gateway?

Check the Block usage option at the threshold value.

wrong.2: The number of threshold values and their blocking status are separate.
wrong.3: Permissions are an issue of management scope and have nothing to do with usage restrictions.

checks.incorrectFeedback: Email or permissions alone are not sufficient to stop usage. Please reconsider what item was responsible for blocking usage at the threshold.

glossary.def: A feature that tracks monthly spending by account, workspace, and tag scope, sends alerts at threshold levels, or blocks requests based on user selection.
An object that monitors credit usage within a warehouse and performs alerts or suspensions based on limits.
A limit applied individually to each user, Snowflake includes blocking functionality, while Databricks uses a per-user threshold within the Unity Gateway budget.
Notifications inform people, while restrictions actually halt requests or warehouses.

misconceptions.myth: Once a budget is set, costs are automatically paused.
misconceptions.fact: Setting only alerts will result in email notifications only. To pause usage, separate restrictions such as Block usage or Suspend must be explicitly configured.

misconceptions.myth: Snowflake's Resource Monitor can also help control the costs of AI services.
misconceptions.fact: Resource Monitor only operates within the warehouse and does not track serverless or AI service expenditures. This area is managed by budget allocations or user-specific quotas.

misconceptions.myth: If the budget range is left empty, nothing is monitored.
misconceptions.fact: When workspaces and tags are left unassigned in Databricks budgets, usage across the entire account is measured.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Databricks budget combines scope, thresholds, and block usage.
Snowflake allocates resource monitoring to warehouses and budgets and user-specific queries to AI services.
Appropriate control measures must be matched to each type of expenditure.
